stories.title: Scores dead in Colombia after powerful earthquake strikes west of country
bullet_points: Quake of 7.4 magnitude collapses and severely damages buildings in several major cities, including Cali and Pereira  More than 100 people died after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia, collapsing and severely damaging scores of buildings in major cities including Cali and Pereira.
The US and Colombian geological surveys reported that a 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck at 7.34am local time on Monday, with its epicentre in the western department of Chocó.
It was felt in neighbouring Venezuela, still reeling from a deadly double earthquake on 24 June.

bullet_points: Operation under way to rescue dozens missing after boat overturned by waves at world’s largest human-made lake  At least 44 people have died   after an overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, police said.

The boat had a capacity of 90 people, but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children, Zimbabwe’s civil protection unit (CPU) said earlier on Wednesday, citing ticket sales.

Ángel Aguirre, who was  arrested last week , is accused of forced disappearance and obstruction of justice for ordering the destruction of surveillance tapes that may have shed light on what happened to the students from the Ayotzinapa teacher training college on the night of 26 September 2014.

stories.title: Halting the march of the African armyworm: a natural cure offers hope to farmers
bullet_points: South African scientist’s breakthrough research shows soil fungus could be used in fight against devastating crop pest  Hearing about fields full of dead caterpillars enveloped in a mysterious white substance intrigued the South African scientist Letodi Luki Mathulwe.
Something was killing off the African armyworm – one of the most devastating pests for farmers in east and southern Africa.
The white substance was a naturally occurring fungus and it was wiping out the caterpillar, which gained its name from its march-like advance through fields of crops.

stories.title: Canadian airline cancels flight after child refuses to wear seatbelt
bullet_points: Flight from Victoria to Toronto forced to return to terminal after repeated attempts to secure child in seat failed  A Canadian airline cancelled a flight from Victoria to Toronto after a child refused to wear a seatbelt.
The child was standing in their chair as the 6 August Porter Airlines flight taxied towards the runway, the airline said.

Repeated attempts by an accompanying parent and crew to secure the child in their seat failed, so the crew elected to return to the terminal and have the two passengers disembark as “the aircraft could not take off in this unsafe condition”, it added.
